Currently tor users are prevented from registering for voat by two means:

1. The registration page explicitly prevents you from registering from a tor exit node ip address. (Tested this morning.)

2. The registration page uses a captcha that requires javascript to be turned on.

The main reasons that I have heard, not from voat staff, but from people expressing genuine beliefs, for disallowing tor users from logging in are:

  1. Spam. People will use tor to make a ton of accounts to spam, troll, or to manipulate voting.

  2. DDOS. People will use tor to flood voat with requests and make the site unusable for everyone.

  3. Quality of person. Tor users are criminals and radicals and we don't want them on our site.

  4. If a tor user posts illegal content, voat will not have any information to give to law enforcement about the user.

And my responses to these points:

  1. Spamming, trolling, and vote manipulations are and will always be concerns whether or not users use tor. These problems are not specific to tor users, and except for "ban the ip address" their mitigation techniques would apply to tor users just as easily as to non-tor users. Does voat really depend on ip banning to stop spammers? Flood filters, moderators, and flagging by regular users should allow detection of spam accounts, from which point the account (not the ip) can be banned. And furthermore, real attackers have no shortage of non-tor ip addresses.

  2. Again, DDOS will always be a concern, but as we have seen many times in the recent past, attackers don't need tor to launch a DDOS attack. Real attackers have no shortage of ip addresses. Moreover, an attacker would do better not to use tor because the tor network is much slower than connecting directly to the internet, thus making the attacker's DDOS much harder (IMO impossible) to perform through tor alone.

  3. The hardcore freedom of speech advocate in me says even criminals and radicals should be allowed to voice their opinions. It should be up to voat users to downvote posts they don't like; that is precisely the point of the voting system in the first place. If we want to curate content, we should do so with our votes, not by banning huge classes of people based on what we think they might post. For those of you that don't care as much about freedom of speech, I can still argue to you. On any given day, there are around 2 million people who use tor. That is a huge number of people to prevent from using voat simply because they value their privacy. Is it really so important to you to stop the tiny fraction of "bad eggs" that you will disagree with? There is a lot of diversity in a userbase that large, and they do not deserve to be blocked because they value their privacy.

  4. Voat should not be conscripted into doing the bidding of law enforcement. If voat happens to have information on a specific crime and wishes to share it with law enforcement, by all means go ahead. But voat should not be required to have personally identifiable information on all its users. Again, over 2 million tor users are prevented from participating in voat. A tiny fraction of them will post illegal content, and in those cases voat will simply ban the account and not have information for law enforcement. So what is worse, not having information for law enforcement (who are certainly capable of tracking serious offenders through other means) in a tiny amount of cases, or preventing 2 million people from using voat based off the fact that they don't want to give out their real ip address?

In case you still aren't convinced that tor users should be allowed, consider some possible compromises:

  1. Allow tor users to register and post content, but do not allow them to vote until they have a substantial amount of CCP.

  2. Disallow registration through tor or posting through tor during perceived DDOS time intervals.

  3. Mark usernames registered through tor with an onion so people know to watch out, and make downvotes count 1.5x more against users that registered through tor unless they have a substantial amount of CCP.

  4. Only allow tor users to make self posts and comments, and remove all links from their comments unless they have a substantial amount of CCP. Attempting to subvert this restriction before having the required CCP would be grounds for an immediate permanent ban.

So what do you think? Can we finally allow tor users to participate?
